text: The pool is a frozen lung, exhaling mist into the grey December sky. Twenty years have eroded the grandeur; the starting blocks are cracked concrete teeth, and the lane markers lie submerged under a skin of ice that traps fallen leaves like amber insects. But look closer. Beneath the frost, shadows dance not from wind, but from memory. A ghostly ripple expands from where a sprinter’s hand once broke the surface, echoing through time. The water, though solid, retains the fluid logic of its former self—currents of cold air swirl in perfect hydrodynamic lines. In the deep end, a single blue plastic cup from a 2036 celebration floats eternally at the edge of thawing, defying gravity’s pull. It is not decay, but preservation. The silence here is loud with the roar of crowds long dispersed, suspended in the crystalline stillness like bubbles caught in resin, waiting for a spring that may never come to break them free.
